Paper_name: Romantic feedbacks influence self-relevant processing: the moderating effects of sex difference and facial attractiveness
Summary: This study investigated how romantic feedback (rejection or acceptance) influences self-relevant processing and how sex differences and facial attractiveness moderate this process. Participants received social feedback from opposite-sex individuals and then completed label-shape pair matching trials. The results showed that romantic rejection inhibited women's self-processing advantage by improving their accuracy for friend-label matching, which was linked to perceived social support. In contrast, men rejected by highly attractive women improved their self-label matching accuracy. Women improved friend-label matching when rejected by highly attractive men or accepted by less attractive men.
Author: Yang Xu, Yuan Yuan, Xiaochun Xie, Hui Tan, Lili Guan
Conclusion: Sex differences and facial attractiveness jointly moderate the influence of romantic feedback on self-relevant processing. Romantic rejection inhibited women's self-processing advantage by shifting attention to friends, linked to seeking social support. Men rejected by highly attractive women showed enhanced self-processing. The findings are associated with sex differences in mating preferences and responses to social threat.
